-- R3: two or more DISTINCT winning suppliers (different UENs) at the same agency share an exact registered address
-- (postal code + block + street + level + unit). One row per award by a supplier in the group.
-- Sole proprietorships/partnerships are excluded: their unit-level address is not published in the committed sample.
-- Params: 'Housing and Development Board' '2024-04-01' '2025-03-31'
WITH won AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT a.agency, x.uen
  FROM gebiz_pg.awards a
  JOIN gebiz_pg.supplier_xwalk x ON x.supplier_name = a.supplier_name AND x.uen IS NOT NULL
  WHERE a.agency = 'Housing and Development Board' AND a.award_date BETWEEN '2024-04-01' AND '2025-03-31'
),
addr AS (
  SELECT w.agency, w.uen,
         concat_ws('|', e.postal_code, upper(e.block), upper(e.street_name), upper(e.level_no), upper(e.unit_no)) AS addr_key,
         concat_ws(' ', e.block, e.street_name, concat('#', e.level_no, '-', e.unit_no), concat('S', e.postal_code)) AS addr_text
  FROM won w
  JOIN ACRA_FILES.entities e ON e.uen = w.uen
  WHERE e.entity_type_description <> 'Sole Proprietorship/ Partnership'
    AND e.postal_code IS NOT NULL AND length(e.postal_code) = 6 AND e.street_name IS NOT NULL AND upper(e.street_name) <> 'NA'
),
grp AS (
  SELECT agency, addr_key, count(DISTINCT uen) AS n_suppliers, min(addr_text) AS addr_text
  FROM addr GROUP BY agency, addr_key HAVING count(DISTINCT uen) >= 2
)
SELECT 'R3' AS flag_id,
       a.tender_no,
       a.agency,
       a.supplier_name,
       x.uen,
       a.award_date,
       a.awarded_amt,
       'suppliers_at_address' AS metric_name,
       g.n_suppliers AS metric_value,
       '2' AS threshold,
       concat('Anomaly for review: ', CAST(g.n_suppliers AS STRING), ' distinct winning suppliers at this agency share the ACRA address ',
              g.addr_text, '. Shared business centres can explain this; requires auditor judgement.') AS detail
FROM gebiz_pg.awards a
JOIN gebiz_pg.supplier_xwalk x ON x.supplier_name = a.supplier_name AND x.uen IS NOT NULL
JOIN addr d ON d.uen = x.uen AND d.agency = a.agency
JOIN grp g ON g.agency = d.agency AND g.addr_key = d.addr_key
WHERE a.agency = 'Housing and Development Board' AND a.award_date BETWEEN '2024-04-01' AND '2025-03-31'
ORDER BY g.n_suppliers DESC, g.addr_text, a.award_date

limitations: R1: Needs a Resolver match (GeBIZ has no UEN). Unresolved names cannot be tested. Newly formed entities are legitimate for many reasons.
R2: ACRA publishes the current status only, so the entity may have been live when it won. Compare award_date with the dates in the underlying registry before concluding anything.
R3: Shared business centres and virtual offices produce benign matches. Address match is on postal code + block + street + level + unit.
R4: GeBIZ here holds tender (ETT) awards only, no quotation (ETQ) records, so splitting below the quotation band is under-detected. Repeat call-offs under a framework can look like splitting.

R5: Embedding similarity is uncalibrated and business descriptions can be broad; always escalated at confidence at most 0.6. Only description pairs with a stored Resolver confidence of at least 0.92 and nonempty descriptions are scored. Run prepare_r5.py after seeding or source changes.

R6: Ten first-match keyword categories are approximate; specialised categories legitimately have few suppliers. Requires at least five distinct category tenders, compares positive award value within the requested agency and period, and groups by supplier name without consolidating aliases.
R8: Our ACRA subset is a candidate set, and renamed or typo'd names may fail to match. Treat as a lead for manual lookup.

R9: Synthetic internal records only; no real evaluation data is used. Compares weighted scores only when every bidder has the same complete criteria and weights, weights sum to one and scores are between 0 and 100. Tied best scores are not flagged; documented award exceptions still require review.

## Limitations
- R1: Needs a Resolver match (GeBIZ has no UEN). Unresolved names cannot be tested. Newly formed entities are legitimate for many reasons.
- R2: ACRA publishes the current status only, so the entity may have been live when it won. Compare award_date with the dates in the underlying registry before concluding anything.
- R3: Shared business centres and virtual offices produce benign matches. Address match is on postal code + block + street + level + unit.
- R4: GeBIZ here holds tender (ETT) awards only, no quotation (ETQ) records, so splitting below the quotation band is under-detected. Repeat call-offs under a framework can look like splitting.
- R5: Embedding similarity is uncalibrated and business descriptions can be broad; always escalated at confidence at most 0.6. Only description pairs with a stored Resolver confidence of at least 0.92 and nonempty descriptions are scored. Run prepare_r5.py after seeding or source changes.
- R6: Ten first-match keyword categories are approximate; specialised categories legitimately have few suppliers. Requires at least five distinct category tenders, compares positive award value within the requested agency and period, and groups by supplier name without consolidating aliases.
- R8: Our ACRA subset is a candidate set, and renamed or typo'd names may fail to match. Treat as a lead for manual lookup.
- R9: Synthetic internal records only; no real evaluation data is used. Compares weighted scores only when every bidder has the same complete criteria and weights, weights sum to one and scores are between 0 and 100. Tied best scores are not flagged; documented award exceptions still require review.
